title: Self-Reported Compute x Misreporting Incentives: Stress-Testing the Honesty Assumption in Compute Governance

original_idea.body:
# Self-Reported Compute x Misreporting Incentives: Stress-Testing the Honesty Assumption in Compute Governance

**Problem:** Compute governance relies on self-reported training compute; incentive to under-report to stay below a threshold makes it unenforceable without an independent estimator.

**Direction:** Build a simple regression linking disclosed params/tokens/benchmark performance to disclosed FLOP, flag outliers as a proof-of-concept compute lie detector.

**Why it matters:** Prototypes independent verification compute governance lacks. Pure public-data analysis.

**Relevant context:** interface-eu.org; Computing Power and Governance (arXiv:2402.08797); Epoch AI compute data.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to enforceable compute governance, a pathway major orgs treat as critical; intermediate estimator independently valuable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple regression on public Epoch data; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (outlier-flagging estimator on public dataset) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure public data, third-party verification niche labs won't build; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Regression on public tabular data; CPU/analytical.

novelty.reasoning: Compute estimation discussed conceptually; a fitted public-data lie-detector may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Independent compute estimation is discussed but a concrete public-data outlier detector may be open.
